The construction never inspects what the algorithm is computing, so it applies to
partial functions and relations verbatim.

total Gap #

Upper bounds — holds for every total

  • \(\mathrm{Q}^{\mathrm{rob}}(\mathrm{PARITY}_n) = \Theta(n)\)
    witness: \(\oplus_n\) BNRdW05
    No $\log n$ overhead, unlike the classical noisy model where $\mathrm{N}_p(\mathrm{PARITY}_n)=\Theta(n\log n)$ [FRPU94, EvansPippenger98]. Quantum error-correction of the oracle is cheaper than classical repetition.

Whether the $\log$ is needed in general is open. Compare with the classical picture in the noise file: there the $\log$ is provably necessary for PARITY.

see also: \(\mathrm{Q}^{\mathrm{rob}}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{N}_{p}(f)\), \(\mathrm{noisyR}(f)\), \(\oplus_n\) data/relations/03-quantum.yaml
relation:
relation Gap #

Upper bounds — holds for every relation

  • \(\mathrm{Q}^{\mathrm{rob}}(f) = O(\mathrm{Q}(f)\log \mathrm{Q}(f))\)
    BNRdW05
    A black-box simulation: amplify each of the $\mathrm{Q}$ queries by $O(\log \mathrm{Q})$ noisy ones and take a (reversible) majority, then union-bound. The construction never inspects what the algorithm is computing, so it applies to partial functions and relations verbatim.
see also: \(\mathrm{Q}^{\mathrm{rob}}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{N}_{p}(f)\), \(\mathrm{noisyR}(f)\), \(\oplus_n\) data/relations/03-quantum.yaml

lo.note:
A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
